prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the 3D geometry of a compact kitchen as the camera wearer turns clockwise from facing the stove counter (0.4 to 0.9 m in front in frames 1–3, with an overhead range hood at 0.3 to 0.5 m above right) to facing an open floor space (1.2 to 1.5 m below) and a microwave cabinet and refrigerator (1.2 to 1.8 m ahead in frames 4–5). In frames 1–2, the wearer's right forearm (0.3 to 0.5 m away) reaches forward onto a pan lid on the stove within arm's reach, while in frame 3 both arms extend (0.3 to 0.5 m) to grasp two small bowls resting ~0.1 m apart on the counter to the left of the pan. Across frames 4–5, as the counter recedes to the far left (0.5 to 1.0 m), the wearer holds both bowls in the near foreground (0.3 to 0.4 m away, ~0.25 m apart) while a second person enters from the bottom right at 0.6 to 0.9 m distance, facing left toward the wearer and extending both arms within reach (0.4 to 0.5 m from the camera) to contact the bowls. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground arms, bowls, and second person's torso from the darker recessed floor and background cabinetry, and highlights the close overhang of the range hood. However, it is unreliable around the upper window blinds and range hood in frames 1–2—which saturate to uniform bright white as if extremely close—and it blurs thin objects like the knife and utensil edges into the counter surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few foreground objects and body parts across the kitchen scene while leaving the cabinetry, sink, microwave, and floor unlabelled. In frames 1–2, it detects the two small bowls on the counter (~0.5 m in front and to the left of the stove, ~0.1 m apart) and a rectangular region over the stove and range hood (~0.4 to 0.8 m to the right), though the wearer's reaching right arm is left only as an unlabelled cutout occluding the stove mask in frame 2. In frame 3, it segments the wearer's two hands entering from the bottom edge (0.3 to 0.4 m away) grasping the two bowls within arm's reach on the counter, along with a knife lying directly between the bowls (~0.5 m away). As the wearer turns right in frames 4–5, the counter and held bowls drop out of the segmentation entirely, and only the second person at the bottom right (0.6 to 0.9 m away, partially out of view at the lower-right frame border) is segmented: first their extended right arm in frame 4, and then their head, torso facing left toward the wearer, and both outstretched arms reaching the wearer's bowls in frame 5. While the map makes the thin knife between the bowls in frame 3 and the exact boundary of the second person's reaching arms in frames 4–5 stand out more distinctly than in the cluttered RGB image, it is highly unreliable in class labelling and recall—misclassifying the red lacquer bowls as 'apple' and 'orange', a small pot as 'cup', and a rectangular crop of the stove area as 'oven', while missing the bowls and the wearer's hands completely in frames 4–5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map is completely blank across frames 1–4 and detects only a single yellow upper-body skeleton in the bottom-right corner of frame 5. In frame 5, this skeleton locates the second person standing roughly 0.6 to 0.9 m in front and to the right of the camera wearer, below the background refrigerator and microwave cabinet (1.2 to 1.8 m away). The arrangement of the head, shoulder, and elbow keypoints shows the person's torso angled to the left toward the camera wearer, with their head tilted slightly down toward the held bowls rather than looking directly up at the camera, and both arms extended forward to ~0.4 to 0.5 m from the wearer (within arm's reach of both people). This skeletal wireframe makes the torso orientation and shoulder-to-elbow geometry of the partially cropped second person easier to read at a glance than in the top-down RGB view. However, the map is largely unreliable for scene-wide spatial understanding because it fails to detect the second person's entering arm in frame 4, misses all magenta hand skeletons for both individuals across all five frames, and never tracks the camera wearer's own reaching arms in frames 1–5.
